Zero-dependency PHP 8.4 micro-framework. Prioritize simplicity, readability, performance, DRY, robust edge handling, clever PHP 8.4 features, and coherent framework-wide design. **Always use `podman compose` (not Docker Compose).** All PHP commands must run inside the `app` container. **Custom test runner, NOT PHPUnit:** [src/Test.php](src/Test.php).

Commands:
podman compose up -d
podman compose exec app php ajo test
podman compose exec app php ajo test --filter=Console
podman compose exec app php ajo test --filter=Job
podman compose exec app php ajo test --parallel
podman compose exec app php ajo test --coverage
podman compose exec app php ajo test --coverage=coverage.xml
podman compose exec app php ajo test --log=junit.xml
podman compose exec app php ajo test:list
podman compose exec app php ajo migrate:install
podman compose exec app php ajo migrate
podman compose exec app php ajo migrate:status
podman compose exec app php ajo migrate:rollback
podman compose exec app php ajo migrate:make create_users_table
podman compose exec app php ajo jobs:install
podman compose exec app php ajo jobs:status
podman compose exec app php ajo jobs:collect
podman compose exec app php ajo jobs:work
podman compose exec app php ajo jobs:prune
podman compose exec app php ajo help
podman compose exec app sh
podman compose logs app
podman compose logs web
podman compose logs db

Tests: direct present-tense names; no “should”; group with `Test::suite()`, cases with `Test::case()`. Use available assertions/hooks; `$state` shares hook/test data.

Each `src/` file has independent Core class plus static facade using Facade trait; singleton by default. Prefer instances in tests. Container supports `set`, `singleton`, `factory`, `get`, `has`.

Pre-release: no backward compatibility concerns; break APIs for better design. Always update tests and docs. Prefer local closures over single-use private methods, match over switch, array functions over loops, guard clauses, `??`/`?:`; omit redundant return types except public API, `:never`, complex types, or clarity. **Always seek the simplest, most direct solution first. Don't over-engineer.** Use built-ins and standard conventions; avoid unnecessary abstractions, obvious docs, brittle tests. Complexity only for real edge cases, complex parsing, or performance-critical code. Optimize with native extensions/shared memory/semaphores; profile first.

Xdebug 3.4.6 is configured in `app`. Use the **xdebug-inspect skill** for instrumented debugging:
/skill xdebug-inspect
podman compose exec app php debug_<issue>.php
